Use PHW styling for every ggplot in the session

Source: R/ggplot.R
use_phw_ggplot.Rd

Call it once at the top of a script, or in the setup chunk of a Quarto document, and every plot after it is in the PHW style with no further code. The R Markdown formats (phw_html_document() and friends) call it for you. It sets:

Usage

use_phw_ggplot(..., palette = NULL)

Arguments

...

Passed to theme_phw(), e.g. base_size = 14 or accessible = TRUE (larger text and thicker lines).

palette

Default qualitative palette for every chart, table and widget, e.g. "accessible" for the colour-blind safe palette. Sets options(phwstyle.palette); see phw_default_palette(). NULL leaves the palette as it is.

Value

The previous theme, invisibly.

Details

  • theme_phw() as the default theme

  • the PHW palette for groups (colour and fill), and PHW blues for continuous and binned colours

  • default colours for layers that don't map a colour: navy bars, areas, lines and points, with text and reference lines in the PHW text colour

  • the PHW font for text and labels

  • the same for geoms from extension packages that are already loaded (see phw_style_extensions()), so load ggrepel, ggridges and the like first

The result is the same on ggplot2 3.5 and 4.0.

After this, add theme_phw() or a scale_*_phw_*() to a plot only to change something for that plot, such as theme_phw(grid = "x") or scale_fill_phw_d(key = "age_group"). Anything you add to a plot wins over these defaults.

Examples

library(ggplot2)
old <- use_phw_ggplot()
ggplot(mpg, aes(class)) + geom_bar()

ggplot(mpg, aes(displ, hwy, colour = drv)) + geom_point()

theme_set(old)
